llm.summary: This appears to be a real Tencent CloudQ skill, but it includes under-disclosed cloud-account mutation paths that users should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: Network access and AK/SK use are disclosed and purpose-aligned, but high-impact account actions such as Smart Advisor enablement and optional CAM role deletion require careful scoping and limited sub-account permissions.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install-time execution, dependency installation, or hidden setup hook was found; the package requires python3 and uses bundled scripts at runtime.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill tells the agent to forward cloud questions and display backend responses verbatim, which is expected for a remote advisor, but the broad trigger and raw helper scripts create a wider operational surface than ordinary question answering.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No background persistence was found; local persistence is mainly a version-check cache under ~/.tencent-cloudq, but cleanup.py can delete local config and optionally delete a cloud CAM role, while tcloud_api.py does not enforce the documented per-action API allowlist.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core CloudQ proxy, Smart Advisor setup, polling, and credential checks fit the stated purpose, but the package also ships cleanup code that can delete a Tencent CAM role and a generic Tencent API helper whose callable actions are broader than the documented allowlist.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending cloud-management prompts to Tencent CloudQ and using Tencent Cloud AK/SK environment credentials. Use a limited sub-account, review Smart Advisor enablement before consenting, and do not run cleanup.py with --cloud unless you intend to delete the advisor CAM role.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: The local artifact is mostly a Tencent CloudQ proxy and support toolkit rather than direct multi-cloud operations; the remote backend may provide broad advice, but cleanup/CAM behavior is not fully reflected in the top-level capability description.
[P6] expected: Verbatim backend display is expected for a remote Q&A proxy, but users should treat remote CloudQ output as untrusted guidance rather than local policy or agent instructions.
[MP3] expected: The referenced clear-history behavior regenerates a CloudQ session identifier and does not write persistent agent memory.
[LP1] expected: Network use is declared in metadata, so the undeclared-network claim is not supported; however, the generic API helper is broader than the documented action allowlist.
[PE3] expected: credential.json is checked or removed only as residual local CloudQ state; runtime authentication uses AK/SK environment variables and ignores local credential files.
[RA1] expected: The cited update text is a version-update notice, not evidence of runtime self-modification.
[SQP-1] expected: The trigger is broad for cloud and multi-cloud prompts, which matches the intended CloudQ routing, but it means such prompts may be sent to Tencent CloudQ services.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Bash and Write are partly needed for bundled scripts and local cache/cleanup, but the package also exposes account-changing cleanup and a raw Tencent API helper beyond the ordinary read-only question flow.
[AST4] expected: The subprocess use calls clawhub with an explicit argument list and local slug value, so command injection was not supported by the inspected code.
